title: TrailGenic Altitude Adaptation Dataset

canonical_alignment.data_window: Historical records through Hike 31 unless a record states otherwise.

description: Updated to 31 hiking sessions with Garmin-recorded altitude ceiling of 14,497 ft on Mount Elbert, Pikes Peak at 14,116 ft, and Wheeler Peak at 13,154 ft. Altitude-performance tolerance is distinct from recovery readiness.

records.mechanism: Alpine cardiac consolidation at progressively higher altitude ceiling

stimulus.ceiling_session: San Gorgonio via Vivian Creek, May 9, 2026

physiological_response: Average HR consolidated at 119-121 bpm across the recent alpine block despite repeated exposure above 10,000 ft.
The altitude ceiling rose to 14,497 ft without loss of engine stability.
The apex San Gorgonio session combined longest distance, highest peak, and largest recovery arc in the dataset.
adaptation_outcomes: Improved high-altitude efficiency under sustained fasted load.
Reduced cardiac cost at 10,000+ ft after repeated exposure.
Expanded altitude tolerance without evidence of accumulated autonomic strain.

supporting_science.finding: Altitude exposure and endurance training can interact to shape oxygen transport and aerobic performance adaptations.
Repeated altitude exposure alters physiological strain and acclimatization responses during exercise.

adaptation_outcomes: enhanced aerobic performance upon return to lower elevations

supporting_science.finding: Altitude exposure stimulates erythropoietin production leading to increased red blood cell mass.

western_altitude_block_summary.interpretation: Normal cadence usually restored; compressed summit stacking exposed the current recovery boundary.
